modules.name: Ground-floor activation and frontage composition
modules.design_question: How much street frontage is active, transparent, fine-grained, sheltered and deep enough to work, and how much is lost to blank wall, lobbies, loading and driveways?
modules.effort: About 8-10 person-days; the edge-annotation UI (category, glazing, entrances, depth, hours) is the main cost; the bike-facility flag adds about 1 day.
inputs: Layer0.Massing: ground-storey volumes (mesh, z from 0 to first-floor underside) with a program tag per volume
Layer0.ProgramTags: office | residential | hotel | retail | cultural_civic | public | amenity | mechanical | core | lobby
SiteContext.StreetEdges (SITE): polylines typed arterial | retail_high_street | lane | mid_block | transit_plaza, plus bike_facility flag (none | painted | protected)
SiteContext.PolicyArea (SITE): Downtown character area (C-5, C-6, HA-1, HA-2) or Granville Street Plan area, chosen by the user; CDDG 4.18 says to refer to it

EdgeAnnotations (user-drawn): per facade segment category (active | semi_active | passive | blank | service), glazing ratio, entrances, egress doors, canopy geometry, active depth, opening hours, grille permeability
Optional: neighbouring frontages for continuity at corners
outputs: FrontageSegments: GeoJSON FeatureCollection<LineString> {street_type, category, length_m, glazing_ratio, entrances_n, depth_m, hours}
ActiveFrontagePct and ActiveDepthOkPct: numbers per street edge
Entrances: Point[] {use, width_m, hours} (consumed by P06-M04 and P06-M05)
BlankRunMax_m, ServiceFrontagePct, WeatherProtectionCoveragePct, NightActivePct: numbers per street edge
VehicleCrossings: {street_id, kind: driveway | loading, over_bike_facility, width_m}[] (to MOBI and P06-M08)
GroundFloorChecks: Check[] {clause_id, source_id, status, value} (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES boards)

parameters.name: Active-use share of street frontage
parameters.relationship: More retail, cafe, civic, transit-entrance or hotel-lobby frontage on streets, corners and plazas -> more activity and visibility; but less frontage for cores, loading and back-of-house, which must move to lanes or below grade.

parameters.name: Entrance spacing
parameters.relationship: Smaller spacing (more doors) -> finer grain and more eyes on the street; each extra door uses frontage and adds tenancies. CDDG S3.1.1a says typically 8.0-12.0 m on non-residential active facades.

parameters.name: Unit (storefront) frontage width
parameters.relationship: Narrower units -> more varied tenants and finer rhythm but less efficient anchors; CDDG expects 7.6-15.3 m fine-grain units, with large uses designed to be demisable later.

parameters.name: Ground-floor glazing ratio
parameters.relationship: Higher transparent share of the ground band -> more visual permeability and surveillance, but more glare and heat gain and less display wall. CDDG says 'most', no percentage; bird-friendly glazing treatment can offset transparency.

parameters.name: Active-use depth behind the facade
parameters.relationship: Deeper active space behind the glass -> real activity and views in, not a 1-2 m display strip or lobby sleeve; but it costs net area and core flexibility. The 9.1 m preset borrows G2.10.2c as an analogue.

parameters.name: Lobby class, opening hours and separate entries
parameters.relationship: CDDG glossary counts hotel lobbies and transit entrances as active uses; office and residential lobbies default semi-active (team). Evening hours and lighting extend activation (G3.1.1b); G2.11.1 asks separate residential entrances.

parameters.name: Blank-wall run length
parameters.relationship: Longer uninterrupted blank wall, grille or egress-door run -> fewer reasons to stop and lower perceived safety; driven by cores, substations, loading and parkade doors placed on streets. Gates and grilles count as blank unless permeable at all hours.

parameters.name: Vehicle crossings and service-door frontage
parameters.relationship: Each driveway or loading door on a street replaces active frontage and adds pedestrian-vehicle conflict; moving access to the lane removes both. Vancouver policy is to minimise width and number of driveways across sidewalks.

parameters.name: Crossings over bike facilities
parameters.relationship: A driveway or loading crossing over a painted or protected bike lane adds cyclist conflict, which the EDM treats with green conflict markings; lane access removes it. Counted apart from pedestrian conflict.

parameters.name: Weather protection depth, height and continuity
parameters.relationship: Deeper, more continuous canopies at 3.0-4.5 m height -> longer rain-sheltered walking and waiting in a wet climate; but they can block daylight and sky view and conflict with street trees.

parameters.name: Ground-storey floor-to-floor height
parameters.relationship: 4.6-6.1 m storeys -> flexible, tall transparent shopfront bands and mezzanines; higher ground storeys raise podium height and construction cost.

parameters.name: Street type and policy area
parameters.relationship: Street type sets how strict the active-frontage target is: continuous on the retail high street, mixed on the arterial, service tolerated on lanes. ODP retail-continuity map and character-area guides (CDDG 4.18) were not opened and may change presets.

metrics.name: Entrance spacing on non-residential active facades
metrics.good: About 8-12 m between entrances (roughly 8-13 entrances per 100 m).
metrics.bad: Gaps above 12 m flagged amber; the guideline says 'typically', so it is discretionary, not pass/fail.
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.1.1a (Appendix A, approved 28 Jul 2026 per City page; final text not yet posted). Per-100 m conversion is ours (derived).
metrics.method: Order entrance points along each street edge; compute gaps; report median, max and entrances per 100 m.

metrics.name: Fine-grain unit frontage width
metrics.good: Ground-level fine-grain active units generally 7.6-15.3 m wide.
metrics.bad: Units wider than 15.3 m that are not designed to be demisable; major anchors are better placed below or above grade.
metrics.basis: CDDG S2.7.2 and G2.7.2 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Measure distance between demising lines or tagged unit boundaries along the facade.

metrics.name: Active frontage share by street type
metrics.good: Retail high street at least 90%; arterial and other streets at least 70%; lanes no minimum (editable presets).
metrics.bad: Below 50% on a retail high street or arterial.
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.6.1 only says to locate active uses on fronting streets, corners, open spaces and mid-block links; no percentage exists. ODP retail-continuity street map not opened.
metrics.method: Length of active segments divided by total street-facing frontage length, per street type.

metrics.name: Active-use depth
metrics.good: Active space at least 9.1 m deep from facade to first core or back-of-house line (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Shallower than the preset, or shelving, signage or back-of-house blocking views in (G3.1.3).
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.10.2c recommends 9.1 m active depth only for frontage of above-grade parking structures; used here as an analogue. G3.1.3 asks interior layouts to keep views in.
metrics.method: Measure perpendicular depth from facade to the first core, back-of-house or opaque line, per active segment.

metrics.name: Lobby and entry classification
metrics.good: Hotel lobbies and transit entrances count active; office and residential lobbies count semi-active unless lined with retail or amenity; residential and non-residential uses have separate entries (G2.11.1).
metrics.bad: A lobby counted as active without a use on its frontage, or one shared entry for residential and other uses.
metrics.basis: CDDG glossary lists hotel lobbies and transit entrances as active uses (verified); the semi-active default for office and residential lobbies is a team assumption.
metrics.method: Read lobby tag, frontage use and entry count per use; reclassify segments before totals.

metrics.name: Night-time activation
metrics.good: Reported only: share of active frontage with evening opening and lighting; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level; long blank or dark runs flagged.
metrics.basis: CDDG G3.1.1b asks for integrated lighting along frontages and G3.1.1c for gates and grilles permeable at all hours; no hours rule exists.
metrics.method: Divide length of segments with evening hours and lighting flag by active frontage length.

metrics.name: Ground-floor transparency ratio
metrics.good: At least 60% glazed in the band from grade to the lower of second-floor underside or canopy soffit (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Below 40% (editable preset).
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.1.1b requires transparent glazing across 'most' of the ground-floor facade, no number. 60% is a placeholder. Bird Friendly Design Guidelines (CDDG 4.8) may reduce effective transparency.
metrics.method: Glazed area divided by facade area in the band; use modelled openings or the annotated ratio.

metrics.name: Longest blank or opaque run
metrics.good: No run longer than about 10 m (about one entrance spacing, editable).
metrics.bad: Run longer than 15 m (editable).
metrics.basis: CDDG G3.1.2 and G2.15.3 say to limit blank walls, grilles, secondary egress doors and opaque glazing along streets, but set no length.
metrics.method: Maximum consecutive length of blank, service or passive segments, with impermeable grilles and gates counted blank.

metrics.name: Weather-protection geometry
metrics.good: Mounting height 3.0-4.5 m; depth-to-height ratio about 0.4-0.7; depth at least 1.5 m in most mixed-use contexts.
metrics.bad: Outside these ranges, or missing over active frontages, transit and entries.
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.2.1 and S3.2.2 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Sample canopy depth and underside height every 2 m along active frontage; compute ratio.

metrics.name: Weather-protection coverage of active frontage
metrics.good: Generally continuous along non-residential active frontages, at least 90% of length (preset).
metrics.bad: Below 50% of length (preset).
metrics.basis: CDDG G3.2.1 asks for generally continuous protection where pedestrian activity is high; the percentages are placeholders.
metrics.method: Canopy length divided by active frontage length.

metrics.name: Vehicle access and service frontage on streets
metrics.good: Vehicle access from the lane; no driveway or loading door on retail high street or arterial frontage where lane access exists.
metrics.bad: Any street-side crossing where lane access is feasible; count and width reported.
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.10.1 (access from lane, away from streets) and Transportation 2040 W 1.1.6 (minimise driveways across sidewalks). No numeric cap exists.
metrics.method: Count vehicle crossings and sum service-door lengths per street edge.

metrics.name: Crossings over bike facilities
metrics.good: No driveway or loading crossing over a bike facility where lane access exists; any crossing counted and flagged for conflict treatment.
metrics.bad: Any such crossing with feasible lane access.
metrics.basis: Extension of CDDG G2.10.1 (verified). EDM 2026 Table 8-18 lists major driveway crossings of bike lanes for green treatment: context, not a limit.
metrics.method: Count crossings whose street edge has bike_facility painted or protected; report width and kind.

metrics.name: Active-storey floor-to-floor height
metrics.good: 4.6-6.1 m for active-use storeys.
metrics.bad: Below 4.6 m for retail, or above 6.1 m without a mezzanine rationale.
metrics.basis: CDDG S2.7.1 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Read storey heights of tagged active volumes.

modules.method: 1) Offset each ground-storey footprint edge facing a street, mid-block link or plaza; split at entrances, demising lines and tag changes. 2) Classify segments as active, semi-active, passive, blank or service from tags, glazing, entrances, lobby class and hours; hotel lobbies and transit entrances count active, office and residential lobbies semi-active (preset). 3) Sum lengths by street type; compute entrances per 100 m, gap distribution, unit widths and longest blank run. 4) Measure active depth from facade to the first core or back-of-house line. 5) Glazing ratio = glazed area over facade area from grade to the lower of second-floor underside and canopy soffit. 6) Sample canopy height and depth every 2 m. 7) Count vehicle crossings and service doors, separately over bike facilities. 8) Look up thresholds in a JSON table where each row carries source id and status. Recompute on any change.
visualization: Plan view: each street edge offset 1 m outward and drawn as a thick polyline coloured by category (active green, semi-active teal, passive amber, blank grey with hatch, service purple), entrances as triangles, 10 m ticks, driveways over bike lanes marked; colour-blind-safe palette plus pattern fills.
Unrolled elevation strip per street (x = length in m, y = grade to second floor) with glazing percentage as a filled line and unit-width bars against the 7.6-15.3 m band.
Bar chart of active percentage per street with preset target line; depth shown as a hatch band behind each segment; one badge per clause linking to the CDDG clause and source id.
Team-assumption metrics drawn with dashed outline and an editable-threshold chip; any later-disproved threshold in the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour.
modules.human_judgment: Whether a use is genuinely active (tenant, hours, display), perceived safety and edge character, material quality at touch distance, and whether a justified breach, such as a civic anchor with a long frontage, beats the rule. The jury may reward justified breaches.
modules.limits: Layer 0 holds no openings, so glazing, depth and entrances need annotation. Activity is inferred from tags, not occupancy. VTC retail-continuity streets and character area are unknown (hypothetical site). CDDG figures are guidelines ('typically'), not by-law limits.

modules.name: Streetwall, podium setbacks and street enclosure
modules.design_question: Do podium height, tower step-back, tower separation, slenderness and floorplate give a street room of comfortable proportion and keep sky and light at the pedestrian level?
modules.effort: About 6-8 person-days; section sampling and lookup tables are simple; multi-tower pairs and context towers need SITE data.
inputs: Layer0.Massing: per-storey footprints and storey heights, with podium/tower split derived from first step-back
Layer0.Towers: each tower's storeys and use portions (employment, hotel, residential)
SiteContext.StreetEdges with right-of-way (ROW) width between building lines, including sidewalks
SiteContext.Buildings and tower sites: existing, approved and potential neighbouring towers, property lines (SITE)
SiteContext.PolicyArea: Downtown character area or Granville Street Plan area chosen by the user (CDDG 4.18)
SiteContext.NorthAngle: rotation of true north relative to the street grid
outputs: StreetSections: {street_id, station_m, podium_h_m, row_w_m, hw_ratio, step_back_m, sky_view_factor}[]
PodiumBandCheck: {street_id, rule: 2.2b | 2.2.7 | 2.2.8, allowed_min_m, allowed_max_m, actual_m, status}
TowerChecks: {pair_type: own-own | own-neighbour | own-property-line, use_pair, separation_m, required_m, status}[]
FloorplateAndSlenderness: {tower_id, floorplate_avg_m2, max_dimension_m, height_to_width}[]
StreetwallContinuityPct per street edge
SkyPlots: stereographic sky maps at sampled eye points (consumed by CLIM and P06-M08)

parameters.name: Podium (streetwall) height
parameters.relationship: Taller podium on a given street -> higher height-to-width ratio, stronger enclosure and less visible sky at the sidewalk (geometry). The CDDG caps podium height by street width so enclosure stays near a fixed band.

parameters.name: Street right-of-way width (building line to building line)
parameters.relationship: Wider street (sidewalks included) -> taller podium allowed for the same enclosure: Downtown tower podiums step from 15.2 m (up to 27.5 m wide) to 15.2-18.3 m (up to 30.5 m) and 18.3-23.0 m above 30.5 m.

parameters.name: Podium cap and exception path
parameters.relationship: Podiums tied to residential use are capped at 18.3 m Downtown (S2.2.7a); S2.2.8b allows 21.3 m on frontage over 60.7 m with enhanced open space. A higher podium shrinks sky but frees ground for open space.

parameters.name: Tower step-back above podium
parameters.relationship: A setback above the podium makes the base read as the street wall and hides tower mass from the sidewalk; the CDDG design tip says a planar change of 1.5-3.0 m is the least that reads as a volumetric break.

parameters.name: Massing variation interval along the street
parameters.relationship: Variation every 25-46 m breaks long monolithic walls into a human-scale rhythm; longer unbroken runs read as monolithic.

parameters.name: Tower floorplate area and dimension
parameters.relationship: Larger floorplate -> wider tower, wider shadow and less sky from the street (geometry). CDDG gives average maxima by use, and a 29.0 m dimension limit for predominantly residential towers.

parameters.name: Tower slenderness
parameters.relationship: Taller, narrower towers read slender and let more sky and sun through; the CDDG design tip says height-to-width of 6:1 to 8:1 or more reads proportionate for tall and very tall towers.

parameters.name: Tower separation by use pair
parameters.relationship: More separation -> more daylight, privacy and sky reaching the public realm. Table 1.5 sets 15.2-24.4 m by use pair; G1.5.1 asks for more where towers exceed typical heights, as 244-305 m towers do.

parameters.name: Intra-site tower spacing and future neighbours
parameters.relationship: Several towers on one block must each meet Table 1.5 against each other; separation is shared equally with a neighbouring tower site (S1.5.1), so a future neighbour needs half the value to the property line.

parameters.name: Corner setbacks at north-south street corners
parameters.relationship: Setting massing back at north-south street corners opens street-end mountain views; the downtown grid is rotated, so 'north-south' must come from the street grid, not true north.

parameters.name: Massing over open space
parameters.relationship: Overhead massing over a POPS is not supported and cuts sun and sky; elsewhere a clear height of 12.0-18.0 m is expected under overhanging mass (S2.2.9).

metrics.name: Podium height versus street width (Downtown tower podiums)
metrics.good: Downtown band by ROW: up to 27.5 m wide, up to 15.2 m; up to 30.5 m, 15.2-18.3 m; over 30.5 m, 18.3-23.0 m. Other contexts up to 15.2 m. Residential-associated podium maximum 18.3 m (S2.2.7a).
metrics.bad: Podium above the band for its street width; needs a written justification.
metrics.basis: CDDG Table 2.2b, S2.2.6-S2.2.8. Table rebuilt from PDF text coordinates (Other-contexts column read as 15.2 m for all rows): recheck against the final CDDG. Which of S2.2.6 or S2.2.7 governs a mixed tower is unresolved.
metrics.method: Look up ROW width, compare podium height from the first step-back; apply the stricter of the band and S2.2.7 when residential floors sit above.

metrics.name: Podium exception for long frontage
metrics.good: Up to 21.3 m where frontage exceeds 60.7 m and enhanced open space is provided (the VTC block qualifies on frontage); show an S2.2.8 chip.
metrics.bad: Above 21.3 m, or 21.3 m without enhanced open space.
metrics.basis: CDDG S2.2.8b and glossary 'Enhanced open space' (at grade, free of overhead buildings). S2.2.8 cross-refers to S2.2.6; the S2.2.7 cap is also exceeded, so applicability is unresolved.
metrics.method: Test block frontage and presence of tagged enhanced open space; then compare podium height with 21.3 m.

metrics.name: Implied podium height-to-width ratio
metrics.good: About 0.55-0.75 for tower podiums at each band's upper width (15.2/27.5, 18.3/30.5, 23.0/30.5); about 1:1 to 1:1.1 for low-rise residential streetwalls (S2.2.2).
metrics.bad: Above the band for the street type.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] Our arithmetic from Table 2.2b; not a quoted rule. The low-rise ratio is quoted from S2.2.2.
metrics.method: Podium height divided by face-to-face ROW width, sampled every 5 m along the street.

metrics.name: Tower step-back above podium
metrics.good: A massing setback above the podium (G2.2.2), with about 1.5-3.0 m planar change to read as a volumetric break.
metrics.bad: Tower faces flush with the podium plane on a street where a defined streetwall is wanted.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] G2.2.2 is a guideline with no number; 1.5-3.0 m is a CDDG design tip about volumetric breaks, not a step-back standard.
metrics.method: Horizontal offset between podium face and first tower storey face.

metrics.name: Average tower floorplate
metrics.good: Employment and hotel towers about 930-1,395 m2; residential baseline 511-670 m2; tall residential up to 746 m2; very tall residential 930-1,115 m2.
metrics.bad: Above the maximum; reviewed case by case.
metrics.basis: CDDG Table 2.3 and S2.3.3. Tall about 90 m, very tall about 150 m (glossary). Splitting a stacked tower's floorplate by use portion is our interpretation.
metrics.method: Slice the mesh at every tower storey and average gross floor area by use portion.

metrics.name: Tower separation by use pair
metrics.good: At or above Table 1.5: residential-residential 24.4; residential-hotel 24.4 (18.3 if S1.5.2 met); residential-employment 18.3; hotel-hotel, hotel-employment, employment-employment 15.2 m.
metrics.bad: Below the table value, unless S1.5.3 (CBD employment or hotel) applies with public-realm light protected; G1.5.2 allows only 0.6-1.0 m.
metrics.basis: CDDG Table 1.5, S1.5.1-S1.5.4, G1.5.1-G1.5.2 (draft Appendix A). Earlier packet omitted residential-hotel and hotel-hotel.
metrics.method: Measure minimum face-to-face distance for every tower pair: own-own and own-neighbour at full value; unbuilt neighbour at half value to the property line; non-tower neighbour per S1.5.4.

metrics.name: Separation for very tall towers (G1.5.1)
metrics.good: Reported only: separation divided by tower height per pair; flag 'consider more' for towers above about 150 m.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: G1.5.1 asks to consider increased separation where towers exceed typical heights but gives no number; VTC towers are 244-305 m.
metrics.method: Divide each pair's separation by the taller tower's height; list pairs.

metrics.name: Tower slenderness indicator
metrics.good: Height-to-width about 6:1 to 8:1 or more for tall and very tall towers.
metrics.bad: Lower ratios flagged for added shaping, articulation or separation.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] CDDG design tip (rule of thumb), not a standard; tall and very tall defined in the glossary.
metrics.method: Tower height divided by the smaller plan dimension of the average floorplate.

metrics.name: Massing variation interval
metrics.good: Variation in massing about every 25.0-45.7 m of frontage.
metrics.bad: Unbroken facade longer than 45.7 m.
metrics.basis: CDDG S2.2.1 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Detect plane changes of at least 1.5 m along the street face and measure spacing.

metrics.name: Streetwall continuity
metrics.good: At least 80% of block-face length within 1 m of the build-to line on the retail high street (preset).
metrics.bad: Below 50% (preset).
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.2.1 says maintain continuity where a continuous streetwall is desired but gives no percentage.
metrics.method: Length of facade within 1 m of the street line at 1.6 m and 12 m heights divided by block-face length.

metrics.name: Sky view factor at sidewalk and street centre
metrics.good: Reported as change from the by-right or existing baseline; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: No Vancouver threshold found; Ewing and Handy 2009 not opened. Earlier 145 unweighted rays replaced by cosine-weighted sampling.
metrics.method: Cast at least 500 cosine-weighted hemisphere rays from 1.6 m eye height (or an analytic view factor); report open-sky fraction.

modules.method: For every street edge cut perpendicular sections every 5 m. Ray-cast left and right from a 1.6 m eye point for facing heights, face-to-face width, podium height (at the first step-back of at least 1.5 m) and step-back. Compare podium height with the Table 2.2b band for the ROW, then the S2.2.7 and S2.2.8 caps. Sample sky view factor with at least 500 cosine-weighted rays. Slice the mesh at each storey above the podium for floorplate area, maximum dimension and slenderness. Measure minimum face-to-face distance for every tower pair: own-own and own-neighbour at full Table 1.5 value, a future neighbour at half value to the property line, a non-tower neighbour per S1.5.4; flag G1.5.1 above 150 m. Measure streetwall continuity with a 2 m buffer of the building line. Thresholds come from versioned lookup tables with source ids.
visualization: Street cross-section drawing per frontage: podium and tower profile, eye-height cone, shaded allowed-podium band for that ROW, and the measured height-to-width ratio labelled.

Plan: each street segment coloured by podium status (inside band green, above band red, no podium grey) with tower footprints and separation lines labelled in metres against required values, intra-site pairs included.
Stereographic sky plot at chosen eye points with percentage of open sky and baseline comparison.
Pass/fail badges linked to CDDG clause numbers; table-reconstruction caveat shown beside Table 2.2b results; derived rows in dashed style.
modules.human_judgment: Perceived enclosure and scale in context, rhythm and proportion of the base, response to heritage or neighbours, skyline and crown quality, and any justified departure from the guideline bands.
modules.limits: Tables 2.2b and 1.5 are discretionary guidelines in draft Appendix A, rebuilt from PDF text. Table 2.2a does not map onto the rotated grid. Sky view factor and wind downwash have no sourced pass level. Character-area guides (4.18) not opened.

modules.name: Public open space: quantity, quality, sun, wind link and access
modules.design_question: Is there enough contiguous public open space, is it sunny, comfortable, furnished and open to everyone, and does the tower's shadow, 600 m to 1.4 km long, spare protected parks and plazas?
modules.effort: About 9-11 person-days: area and POPS checks 2, protected-space shadow projection 4, on-site sun-hours raster 2, Basic and Detailed study reports with the special-case table 2.
inputs: Layer0.Massing and SiteBoundary
GroundPlane polygons tagged POPS | mid_block | plaza | transit_plaza | retail_patio | park_dedication | private
Seating objects (type, back flag, fixed or moveable), tree canopy polygons
SiteContext.Context: built, approved and known proposed buildings with heights, plus terrain (City study rule, section 5)
SiteContext.ProtectedSpaces: Table 1 polygons with class and special-case id; Davie and Robson north-sidewalk strips (SITE)
SolarSettings: dates (22 Sep; 11 Nov for Victory Square), UTC offset (-7 default, -8 variant), study type Basic or Detailed
CLIM: pedestrian wind comfort class grid at 1.5 m (if available); shadow engine optional as cross-check
AccessAttributes per space: free | ticketed, opening hours, SRW (statutory right-of-way) yes/no

ShadowDomain: {radius_m, h_max_m, el_min_deg, spaces_in_reach[]}
ShadowStudy: {space_id, rule_id, study, instants[], existing_m2, added_m2, cumulative_m2, coverage_pct, default_verdict}[]
SunHoursGrid: direct-sun hours (0-6 h) on own POPS cells, 0.5 m
SeatingSupply: {m_per_100m2, types_n, fixed_backs_pct, moveable_chairs_n}
OpenSpaceChecks and WindPointChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES)

parameters.name: Public open space share of site area
parameters.relationship: More public open space (POPS, mid-block links, plazas) -> more room for gathering, trees and sun; but less building footprint. VTC block is about 11,468 m2: 20% is about 2,294 m2, a POPS of about 10% about 1,147 m2.

parameters.name: POPS shape, contiguity and size
parameters.relationship: A contiguous space of about 300 m2 or more with 1:1-1:2 proportions is usable as a neighbourhood space; narrow or fragmented leftovers do not qualify and read as private.

parameters.name: Overhead massing and podium location of the space
parameters.relationship: Mass over a POPS removes it from the POPS count and cuts sun and sky; space on podium or roof without public stairs and lifts also does not count.

parameters.name: Tower height, floorplate and position relative to protected spaces
parameters.relationship: Taller, wider tower south or west of a space -> longer, wider shadow -> fewer sunlit hours there. Reach is H / tan(sun elevation): about 600 m for 305 m on 22 Sep (27 degrees at 10:00), about 1.4 km on 11 Nov.

parameters.name: Test date, time window and UTC offset
parameters.relationship: Each protected space has its own date and window (22 Sep 10:00-16:00; Robson Village to 15:00; Victory Square cenotaph 11 Nov 10:00-12:00). The offset moves each instant by an hour, which changes the shadow cast.

parameters.name: Study type: Basic or Detailed
parameters.relationship: Basic (two-hour instants) is for every applicant; Detailed (15-minute, 25 instants, area take-offs, coverage %) is needed to argue an exception. Running Detailed early shows the shadow budget but costs run time.

parameters.name: Wind exposure at grade points
parameters.relationship: Taller towers and open corners tend to raise ground wind at seating, entrances, sidewalks, transit plaza, links and terraces -> fewer comfortable hours. CDDG G1.8.1b says site open space to minimise wind exposure.

parameters.name: Wind-mitigation geometry (podium edge, canopy, step-back)
parameters.relationship: A podium step-back, canopy width and corner shaping may deflect downwash from the base before it reaches the sidewalk; effect size is unsourced and belongs to CLIM testing.

parameters.name: Seating quantity and type
parameters.relationship: More seating with backs, in sun and shade, at corners and links -> longer stays and wider use by older people. NYC rule: 1 linear ft per 30 sq ft, three types above 465 m2, moveable seating above 929 m2.

parameters.name: Retail patio share of a POPS
parameters.relationship: More private patio inside a POPS -> less space and less perceived publicness; CDDG limits patios to about one third of a POPS.

parameters.name: Access hours and legal tenure (SRW)
parameters.relationship: Longer, unconditional hours and a statutory right-of-way -> the space works as public; early closing or gates reduce use. NYC default is open at all times, with limited closings only by authorisation.

parameters.name: Planting, soil volume and underground setbacks
parameters.relationship: Underground setbacks and slab drops enable in-ground trees, shade and habitat; CDDG asks tree planting in plazas where contiguous planted areas or setbacks exist, with soil depths per the CSLA standard (S4.5.1).

parameters.name: Transit plaza size
parameters.relationship: Space next to a station entrance sized for waiting and circulation (about 6.1 m by 6.1 m at least) supports transit use; it is not counted as park dedication.

metrics.name: Public open space as share of site area
metrics.good: At least 20% of site area (about 2,294 m2) as public open space, counting POPS, mid-block links and plazas; vehicle space excluded.
metrics.bad: Below 20%. The 10% mid-sized-site target (S1.9.2) does not apply to an 11,468 m2 block; park dedication may be requested.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.9.1 and glossary: 'Public open space' includes POPS and mid-block connections; 'Mid-sized sites' 4,000-8,000 m2; 'Large sites' refer to the Large Developments policy (8,000 m2 site or 45,000 m2 floor area in 2013 report; current text not opened).
metrics.method: Sum tagged public open space meeting counting rules; divide by 11,468 m2.

metrics.name: POPS component of the open-space total
metrics.good: POPS about 10% of site area (about 1,147 m2) on non-residential tower sites with frontage over 60.7 m (VTC qualifies); counts toward the 20% total.
metrics.bad: Below about 10%, fragmented or under mass.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.10.2 and glossary (POPS is a public open space). Whether S1.10.2 is extra to or inside the 20% is unresolved; tool counts it inside.
metrics.method: Area of eligible POPS polygons divided by site area.

metrics.name: POPS geometry and eligibility
metrics.good: Contiguous, proportion 1:1 or 1:2, area about 300 m2 or more, secured by SRW, free of overhead massing; excludes setbacks, engineering SRWs, vehicle space, and podium or roof areas without public stairs and lifts.
metrics.bad: Fragmented, under mass, without SRW or access points.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.11.1 and glossary definition of POPS.
metrics.method: Apply eligibility filters to tagged polygons; compute minimum bounding rectangle aspect.

metrics.name: Shadow analysis domain
metrics.good: Radius at least H / tan(lowest sun elevation in the window): about 600 m for 305 m on 22 Sep (UTC-7); about 1.4 km on 11 Nov at UTC-7, 0.9 km at UTC-8.
metrics.bad: A fixed small radius that omits protected spaces within reach.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] Our NOAA-algorithm calculation at 49.28 N: elevation 26.9 degrees at 10:00 and 28.1 at 16:00 on 22 Sep; 12.6 degrees at 10:00 on 11 Nov (UTC-7).
metrics.method: R = H_max / tan(el_min) over the instants of each rule; keep Table 1 spaces within R; report R in the UI.

metrics.name: Direct sun on own public open space
metrics.good: At least 50% of POPS area has 2 or more hours of direct sun on 22 Sep between 10:00 and 16:00 (UTC-7) (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Less than 25% of area reaches 2 hours (editable preset).
metrics.basis: Vancouver sets the window but no minimum sun for private open space. The 2-hour, 50% test follows BRE BR 209 practice (recalled, not opened), which uses 21 March; moved here to 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00.
metrics.method: Test 0.5 m cell centres against unioned shadow polygons at 25 instants; hours = trapezoid sum (end weights 0.5) times 0.25 h, so the maximum is 6.0 h.

metrics.name: New shadow: parks, school sites, Dilawri Square South, Jack Poole Plaza, Robson Square
metrics.good: No new shadow within property lines on 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00 (UTC-7).
metrics.bad: FAIL by default. Exception path (3.1.2): public benefit, shadow rationale statement, Detailed study; staff weigh 3.1.3 items.
metrics.basis: Solar Access Guidelines (memo RTS 16506, Appendix A) 3.1.1-3.1.3, 4.2.1 and Table 1 classes.
metrics.method: Project shadow per instant, union, intersect with the space polygon; any added area above numerical tolerance fails.

metrics.name: New shadow: Dr Sun Yat-Sen Gardens and Park
metrics.good: No new shadow at any time between 10:00 and 16:00 on 22 Sep.
metrics.bad: FAIL. Section 4.1 states no exception path; whether 3.1.2 applies is unresolved.
metrics.basis: Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 4.1.1 ('despite' 3.1) and Table 1 (Local park, refer to 4.1).
metrics.method: As for parks; Basic study at two-hour instants plus a finer check.

metrics.name: New shadow: Victory Square and Cenotaph circle
metrics.good: No new shadow in the park (3.1.1) and none on the Cenotaph circle 10:00-12:00 on 11 Nov.
metrics.bad: FAIL. Exception only after comprehensive public and key stakeholder engagement (4.3.2). Run 11 Nov at UTC-8 and UTC-7 because the text says PST.
metrics.basis: Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 4.3.1-4.3.2 and Table 1 (urban plaza, refer to 4.3). 4.3.1 applies in addition to the 3.1 rules.
metrics.method: Second solar date; shadow polygons on the Cenotaph circle for both offsets.

metrics.name: New shadow: Davie and Robson Village north sidewalks
metrics.good: No new shadow on the north sidewalk, curb to property line: Davie 10:00-16:00, Robson 10:00-15:00 on 22 Sep.
metrics.bad: FAIL by default. Exception path 3.3.2: public benefit, shadow rationale, Detailed study of affected blocks.
metrics.basis: Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 3.3.1-3.3.3, Maps 2 and 3.
metrics.method: Intersect shadow union with the sidewalk strip polygons per instant.

metrics.name: New shadow: West End miniparks and other urban plazas
metrics.good: Report added shadow and explore strategies to minimise it where possible; no pass or fail.
metrics.bad: Added shadow with no mitigation record.
metrics.basis: Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 3.2.1. Earlier packet put every urban plaza here; Jack Poole Plaza, Robson Square, Dilawri South and Victory Square are special cases.
metrics.method: Same projection; verdict is 'minimise' (amber), never a hard fail.

metrics.name: Study type and coverage formula
metrics.good: Basic study (10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00) for every application; Detailed study (25 instants, area take-offs, coverage %) when an exception to 3.1.1 or 3.3.1 is argued.
metrics.bad: Detailed omitted when an exception is argued, or the 15-minute run presented as the standard test.
metrics.basis: Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 5.1.1 and 5.2.1. Coverage % = total shadow area over 25 instants / (space area x 25), as the City defines it.
metrics.method: Basic: 4 instants. Detailed: 25 instants; existing, added and cumulative m2 per instant; City coverage formula.

metrics.name: Study inputs and time base
metrics.good: Model set to Pacific Time as UTC-7 with complete built and approved context, known proposed developments and topography; new shadow shown apart from existing; trees and small structures excluded from baseline.
metrics.bad: Context, proposed buildings or terrain missing, or a seasonal offset used.
metrics.basis: Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, section 5 (PDT, UTC-7); Council report RTS 18459 App. D replaces PDT with PT after BC adopted permanent daylight time. Victory Square text still says PST.
metrics.method: Fix UTC-7 in the solar routine, show the offset in the UI, include proposed and approved buildings and terrain.

metrics.name: Seating supply
metrics.good: 1 ft per 30 sq ft (about 10.9 m per 100 m2); two types, three above 465 m2; at least 50% of fixed seating with backs; moveable chairs above 929 m2; seating at corners and links.
metrics.bad: Less than half of the NYC quantity, or no seating at corners and links.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] NYC ZR 37-741: text verified, not a Vancouver rule; adopted as a team preset. CDDG G3.4.2 supports seating at corners and mid-block links.
metrics.method: Sum linear seating metres by type and plaza area; count backs on fixed seating; moveable chairs at 1 per 18.6 m2.

metrics.name: Wind comfort at grade points
metrics.good: No sourced criterion; report CLIM comfort class per point type: seating, entrances (M01), sidewalk segments (M05), transit plaza and links (M04), terraces (M07).
metrics.bad: Strolling class or worse at seating or entrances (placeholder).
metrics.basis: No Vancouver wind criterion opened; thresholds belong to CLIM. CDDG G1.8.1b (verified, qualitative) and the 1997 Higher Buildings Policy ask for no adverse wind or microclimate effect.
metrics.method: Intersect CLIM comfort-class grid with each point set; report class shares; mark 'unverified until CLIM sources exist'.

metrics.name: Access hours and tenure
metrics.good: Public open space secured by SRW and open at least from 7:00 to 22:00 in summer and 7:00 to 20:00 in winter; mid-block links 24 hours (preset).
metrics.bad: Hours shorter than the NYC allowed-closing schedule, ticketed entry, or no SRW.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] CDDG requires SRWs for POPS and links but states no hours; hours come from the NYC authorised-closing schedule (ZR 37-727).
metrics.method: Read access attributes; compare to the schedule.

metrics.name: Retail patio share of POPS
metrics.good: Patios no more than about one third of the POPS; signage states public use.
metrics.bad: Above one third, or no public-use signage.
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.6.1 and S3.6.2.
metrics.method: Patio area divided by POPS area.

metrics.name: Transit plaza minimum size
metrics.good: At least about 6.1 m by 6.1 m beside a station entrance.
metrics.bad: Smaller, or counted toward park dedication.
metrics.basis: CDDG S4.4.1 and G1.9.1.
metrics.method: Largest inscribed rectangle in the plaza polygon.

modules.method: 1) Tag ground-plane polygons; apply CDDG counting rules (remove setbacks, engineering SRWs, vehicle areas, area under mass, elevated areas without public stairs or lifts); report share of 11,468 m2. 2) Compute solar position (NOAA algorithm, fixed UTC offset) for each rule's date and window. 3) Size the domain R = H / tan(lowest elevation); keep Table 1 spaces within R. 4) Project each building to a shadow polygon per instant (convex hull of footprint and footprint shifted H / tan(elevation) along the shadow azimuth; edge sweeps for non-convex), union, intersect with each space for take-offs and City coverage %. 5) For own POPS test 0.5 m cell centres against the union; integrate sun hours (trapezoid). 6) Run in the browser (Pyodide: shapely, numpy); raster only on site. 7) Sum seating; intersect CLIM wind grid with point sets.
visualization: Ground-plane false-colour mesh of direct-sun hours with a 0-6 h legend, a bold contour at 2 h, POPS outlines hatched, seating points on top, and a 15-minute time scrubber from 10:00 to 16:00.
Shadow-reach disc around the site with Table 1 spaces inside it, coloured by rule (no-new-shadow red when breached, minimise amber), and the radius labelled.
Protected-space panel: stacked area chart of existing and added shadow percent against time, with the City coverage percentage printed; Basic and Detailed tabs.

Horizontal bars of public open space percent against 10% and 20% lines, and pass/fail badges linked to CDDG and solar-guideline clauses; team-assumption rows dashed, external benchmarks in their own style.
modules.human_judgment: Programming and stewardship, who the space feels welcome to, perceived safety, relation to Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh place-making, park dedication versus POPS (decided by City and Park Board), and whether a shadow trade-off is justified by public benefit.
modules.limits: Sun uses clear-sky geometry; Vancouver is often overcast in fall. Trees and small structures are ignored, as in the City baseline. v1 treats each space as a flat plane, not full topography. CDDG space targets are guidelines; stacking of 20% and POPS 10% is unresolved.

modules.name: Permeability, mid-block connections and block structure
modules.design_question: Does the block give direct, legible, step-free-ready public routes through it, and does the below-grade station link work as public realm, not just as a graph edge?
modules.effort: About 6-8 person-days; graph and width checks are simple; directness and link-quality checks need the station entrance location.
inputs: SiteBoundary and SiteContext.StreetNetwork (streets, lanes, existing mid-block links) from OSM or City open data
Layer0.Massing and ground-plane passage polylines with clear width, open-to-sky flag, hours and SRW flag
SiteContext.TransitEntrances: existing station entrance and the required below-grade secondary entrance (from MOBI packet or site plan)
SiteContext.BelowGradeLink: drawn path, clear width, lifts, stairs, level changes, sightline points to grade and concourse (user or MOBI)
Destinations: retail high street, arterial crossings, parks, plazas (from SITE packet)
outputs: WalkGraph: NetworkX graph {nodes: entrances, junctions; edges: length_m, clear_width_m, open_to_sky, hours}
ConnectionChecks: {connection_id, required, clear_width_m, min_required_m, status}[]
LinkQualityChecks: Check[] for the below-grade link (G4.4.1 and G4.4.2 items)
DirectnessTable: {from, to, network_m, straight_m, prd}[] (PRD = pedestrian route directness)
Isochrones: polygons for 2-, 5- and 10-minute walks from the station entrance
RouteGraph for P06-M05 (flows) and P06-M06 (step-free routing)

parameters.name: Number and location of mid-block connections
parameters.relationship: More public through-routes -> shorter walks, more route choice and more active edges; each link removes buildable area. CDDG requires one where the site is adjacent to or includes a station entrance.

parameters.name: Connection width (building face to building face)
parameters.relationship: Wider links feel safer and allow daylight and active edges but cost site area. For the VTC block S1.12.2c sets 9.1 m face to face; 2.4 m clear path (S3.8.1). 4.5, 5.4 and 7.3 m apply to other cases.

parameters.name: Open to sky versus covered breezeway
parameters.relationship: Covered links need height-to-width of at least 2:1, active edges, a direct line and public hours or they read as tunnels; open-to-sky links are the default.

parameters.name: Alignment with desire lines and destinations
parameters.relationship: Links that join the station, parks and high street pick up existing pedestrian flows; links to nowhere stay empty and unsafe.

parameters.name: Route directness (network over straight-line distance)
parameters.relationship: Detours above straight-line distance raise walking time and reduce use; connected street networks are positively associated with physical activity in a meta-analysis (mainly children).

parameters.name: Hours of public access of each link
parameters.relationship: Links closed outside building hours cut the network at night; breezeways may be limited to building hours by the CDDG, mid-block links secured by SRW are public.

parameters.name: Grade separation of the transit link
parameters.relationship: A below-grade secondary entrance takes crowds off the surface but needs lifts, stairs, active uses and a visual link to the concourse to stay legible.

parameters.name: Lifts, stairs and level changes on the below-grade link
parameters.relationship: More than one lift keeps the link step-free when one fails; fewer level changes shorten the trip. CDDG G4.4.2b asks at least an elevator and a staircase.

parameters.name: Active edges and sightlines along the link
parameters.relationship: Active uses lining the link, with views to grade and the concourse, make it legible and safer; a blank tunnel deters use (G4.4.2c-d).

metrics.name: Mid-block connection required by station adjacency
metrics.good: At least one public connection provided where the site includes or adjoins a station entrance.
metrics.bad: No connection although the trigger applies.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.1b and G1.12.2 (draft Appendix A). The VTC brief requires a secondary transit entrance, so the trigger applies.
metrics.method: Check presence and endpoints of connections against station entrance location.

metrics.name: Connection width
metrics.good: VTC preset: at least 9.1 m building face to building face (station-adjacent large site) with a 2.4 m clear path.
metrics.bad: Narrower: show a 'G1.12.1 variation, justify' chip, not a pass. Context rows only: 4.5 m face to line when the neighbour delivers half; 5.4 m non-residential; 7.3 m voluntary.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.2c (large sites or sites identified in S1.12.1), S3.8.1 clear path; variations by G1.12.1.
metrics.method: Minimum distance between facing facades along the link centreline.

metrics.name: Open to sky or compliant breezeway
metrics.good: Primarily open to sky; a breezeway only if height-to-width at least 2:1, lined with active uses, direct and public, open during building hours.
metrics.bad: Enclosed passage not meeting these tests.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.4 and S2.2.10.
metrics.method: Compute roofed share and height-to-width of each link.

metrics.name: Below-grade link: elevator and staircase
metrics.good: At least one elevator and one staircase on each integrated station entrance.
metrics.bad: Stair only or lift only.
metrics.basis: CDDG G4.4.2b (applies where a development includes integrated station entrances).
metrics.method: Count tagged lifts and stairs on the link graph.

metrics.name: Below-grade link: lift redundancy
metrics.good: At least two lifts on the link so one outage does not break step-free access (editable preset).
metrics.bad: A single lift.
metrics.basis: CDDG asks only 'an elevator'; redundancy is a team assumption pending TransLink input (MOBI).
metrics.method: Count lifts serving the same level change.

metrics.name: Below-grade link: active uses and visual connection
metrics.good: Active uses next to the secondary entrance and on the concourse level; strong visual connection to the concourse and below-grade active uses; consider washrooms.
metrics.bad: Blank link, or no sightline between grade and concourse.
metrics.basis: CDDG G4.4.2c-e (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Share of link edge tagged active; ray test from grade entrance to concourse points.

metrics.name: Station overbuild and plaza checklist
metrics.good: Where a development includes a station overbuild or primary headhouse: items a-h of G4.4.1 (full footprint overbuild, continuous streetwall, complementary paving, seating, shade, services integrated, multiple doors).
metrics.bad: Items missing without a reason.
metrics.basis: CDDG G4.4.1 (applies only with station overbuild); the VTC brief may not include one.
metrics.method: Manual checklist with evidence note per item.

metrics.name: Route directness between key pairs
metrics.good: At most 1.25 for station to high street, and across-block pairs (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Above 1.5 (editable preset).
metrics.basis: No sourced Vancouver or other threshold was opened. Transportation 2040 notes the grid gives direct walking routes.
metrics.method: Shortest path length on the walk graph divided by straight-line distance.

metrics.name: Longest stretch of block perimeter without a public through-route
metrics.good: At most about 100 m (editable preset); the VTC long side is 144.8 m, so one link near the middle gives about 72 m.
metrics.bad: Above 150 m (editable preset).
metrics.basis: No sourced block-length rule was found for Vancouver; this is a starting value.
metrics.method: Distance between consecutive public openings along the block perimeter.

metrics.name: Public access tenure of required links
metrics.good: Required links secured by SRW and open to the public.
metrics.bad: No SRW or access limited to a private operator's hours.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.3 asks an SRW; 24-hour opening is not stated.
metrics.method: Read SRW flag and hours attribute.

metrics.name: Below-grade link width and daylight
metrics.good: Reported only: clear width and daylight or sky view at grade openings; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: CDDG gives no width or daylight value for station links; TransLink standards not opened (MOBI packet).
metrics.method: Minimum clear width along the drawn link; count of openings to grade.

metrics.name: Street intersection density (context scale)
metrics.good: Reported only; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: Street intersection density is positively associated with physical activity in a systematic review (mainly children); LEED ND thresholds not opened.
metrics.method: OSMnx intersections within 800 m of the site divided by area.

modules.method: Build a walk graph from streets, lanes, sidewalks, mid-block links, building passages and the below-grade link, each edge carrying length, clear width, open-to-sky flag and hours. Check each connection against the 9.1 m VTC width and sky-openness tables. Compute shortest paths between station entrance(s), high-street midpoint, arterial crossings and each public entrance from P06-M01; divide by straight-line distance for directness. Compute 2-, 5- and 10-minute walk areas at a preset speed. Compute the longest perimeter stretch without a public through-route. Score the below-grade link against G4.4.2 (elevator and stair, active edges, sightline) and G4.4.1 where overbuild applies. Optionally compute context intersection density and space-syntax integration.
visualization: Plan with the walk graph drawn over the block: edges coloured by clear width (below 2.4 m red, 2.4-9.1 m amber, 9.1 m and over green for links), open-to-sky edges solid and covered edges dashed.
Isochrone rings (2, 5, 10 minutes) from the station entrance, shaded by time, with labelled route directness for the three key pairs.
Section strip of the below-grade link: lifts, stairs, active edge share and the sightline to grade and concourse drawn and checked.
Perimeter ruler around the block marking public openings and the longest gap; pass/fail badges linked to CDDG clauses; team-assumption rows editable.
modules.human_judgment: Legibility and sightlines, whether the link feels public rather than private, night-time safety, wayfinding including Indigenous place names, and negotiation with TransLink and the neighbouring site for the secondary station entrance.
modules.limits: Pure geometry: it does not model crowding, weather or pedestrian choice. Route directness and block-gap thresholds are presets without a source. Walking speed is a preset. The below-grade link must be drawn by the user; Layer 0 may not include it.

modules.name: Sidewalk capacity and pedestrian level of service
modules.design_question: At peak times and in short surges, are sidewalks, crossings and corners around the block wide enough for comfortable walking once furniture, queues and station flows are counted?
modules.effort: About 5-7 person-days for static footway and crossing comfort with sensitivity bands; agent-based simulation (roadmap) adds about 8-10 days.
inputs: StreetSections: sidewalk total width, building edge, trees, furniture, bike racks, canopy posts (SITE and user sections)
P06-M01 Entrances and program GFA by use from Layer 0
MOBI: station and bus-stop flows (persons per peak hour and peak 15 minutes) at the transit entrances
P06-M07 PublicLiftQueue: queue persons and area at the street-level public lift lobby
PedestrianDemandPreset: person trips per 100 m2 GFA by use, peak-hour share, walk share, low/central/high multipliers (editable team assumptions)
Street area type: high street | office and retail | residential | tourist attraction | transport interchange; crossing signal timings
outputs: FootwayComfort: {segment_id, flow_pph, flow_peak15_pph, ppmm, pcl_class, area_type_verdict, clear_width_m, required_width_m}[]
WidthBudget: stacked widths building buffer + active zone + clear + furniture + kerb buffer
CrossingComfort: {crossing_id, arm_pcl, island_rows}[]
CornerQueueAreas: polygons with area per person
PCLChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08)

parameters.name: Peak-hour and peak 15-minute pedestrian flow
parameters.relationship: More office, retail and hotel floor area, and closer transit -> higher peak flows on adjacent sidewalks; end-of-day egress and train surges exceed the hourly mean. Rates per m2 are team assumptions.

parameters.name: Effective clear width
parameters.relationship: Total width minus 0.2 m building and kerb buffers and furniture buffers -> flow per metre rises as obstacles are added; one bench or tree pit can drop comfort a class.

parameters.name: Flow per metre of width (ppmm)
parameters.relationship: Pedestrians per minute per metre of effective width: higher values mean more bumping and slower walking, from under 3 ppmm (A+) to over 35 ppmm (E).

parameters.name: Area type and tolerance
parameters.relationship: High streets and tourist attractions tolerate least crowding; residential is intermediate; office/retail and interchange tolerate most. The area type sets the pass floor; B+ is the recommended level everywhere.

parameters.name: Static activity (queues, window shoppers, cafe seating)
parameters.relationship: People standing or sitting use width that walkers cannot; patios and displays can reduce clearway below 2.4 m if not allowed for in the boulevard.

parameters.name: Building setback or SRW widening
parameters.relationship: Setting the building back adds clear width at no street cost; commercial corridors have been asked for at least 5.5 m from back of curb (1.0 m back boulevard, 3.0 m clear, 1.5 m front boulevard).

parameters.name: Transit arrival surges
parameters.relationship: Train arrivals deliver short, high peaks at station entrances; check peak 15 minutes and, for interchange segments, TfL's average-of-maximum level rather than the hourly mean.

parameters.name: Crossing time and corner waiting
parameters.relationship: Shorter signal time available to cross raises relative flow on the crossing arm; wider corners and islands give waiting people more space. TfL: more than three queue rows on an island pushed people to cross outside it.

parameters.name: Demand sensitivity band
parameters.relationship: Low, central and high demand multipliers show which width decision holds across plausible rates; a design that fails only in the high case is a judgment call, not a fault.

metrics.name: Pedestrian Comfort Level by area type
metrics.good: B+ or better recommended everywhere (11 ppmm or fewer). Pass floor at peak: high street and tourist B; residential B-; office/retail and interchange C+.
metrics.bad: At risk: high street and tourist B-; residential C+; office/retail and interchange C-. Unacceptable below those. Never below C+ even with compensation.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] TfL Pedestrian Comfort Guidance (2010) Figures 8-9; London research, text verified, not adopted by Vancouver. Figure 9 decoded from its colour fills: confirm visually.
metrics.method: ppmm = pph / 60 / clear width; map to the PCL table and the area-type row for the segment.

metrics.name: Peak-hour and peak 15-minute check
metrics.good: Both peak hour and peak 15 minutes meet the area-type floor; interchange segments also pass TfL average-of-maximum where available.
metrics.bad: Fails only in the 15-minute surge: widen or add queue space.
metrics.basis: Hourly means hide egress and train surges; the 15-minute proxy is a team preset. TfL's average-of-maximum multiplier sits inside its spreadsheet and was not opened.
metrics.method: Run the PCL calculation for the peak hour, the busiest 15 minutes and the low, central and high multipliers.

metrics.name: Clear sidewalk width, Vancouver standard
metrics.good: Commercial and mixed-use streets: at least 3.0 m clear, wider by volume; downtown clearways of 3.0-5.0 m exist; 4.0 m for new high-volume corridors.
metrics.bad: Below 2.4 m (the constrained minimum) or below 3.0 m on commercial streets without City Engineer agreement.
metrics.basis: Engineering Design Manual 2026, Section 8.4.3.1 and Table 8-3.
metrics.method: Read clear width from the section after removing furniture and patio encroachment.

metrics.name: Pedestrian realm depth from back of curb
metrics.good: About 5.5 m (1.0 m back boulevard + 3.0 m clear + 1.5 m front boulevard) on commercial corridors.
metrics.bad: Below that without a City Engineer-approved reason.
metrics.basis: Engineering Design Manual 2026, Section 8.4.3.1 (historic request for redevelopment projects).
metrics.method: Measure back of curb to property line plus SRW.

metrics.name: Recommended total footway width by flow class
metrics.good: Under 600 pph: 2.9 m; 600-1,200: 4.2 m; 1,200-2,000: 5.3 m (3.3 m without furniture). Above 2,000 pph derive clear width = pph / 60 / 11 (B+ ceiling), plus 0.2 m buffers and furniture.
metrics.bad: Below the recommended width; above 2,000 pph the table no longer applies.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] TfL Appendix B (widths comfortable up to 2,000 pph); the above-2,000 rule is our derivation from the B+ band.
metrics.method: Classify segment flow; compare total width, or compute required clear width from ppmm.

metrics.name: Crossing arm and island comfort
metrics.good: Crossing arm better than C-; island queue at most three rows; relative pph = pph / share of time available to cross.
metrics.bad: Arm at C-, D or E (TfL mitigation trigger), or more than three queue rows.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] TfL crossing method (Step 2): text verified, London signals, not adopted locally.
metrics.method: Compute relative pph and ppmm on each arm and island from signal timings; count queue rows.

metrics.name: Corner queue area per person
metrics.good: Reported only: area per waiting person at corners and the transit entrance; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: Fruin queueing densities were not opened; TfL gives crossing island rows only.
metrics.method: Corner polygon area minus furniture, divided by peak waiting persons.

metrics.name: Footway minimum and obstacle gaps
metrics.good: Footway at least 2.0 m (1.5 m acceptable under constraint); gaps at obstacles at least 1.0 m and no longer than 6 m.
metrics.bad: Below these.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] UK DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2; text verified, not adopted by Vancouver.
metrics.method: Scan sections for obstacle gaps.

metrics.name: Street-furniture placement
metrics.good: Furniture set back to keep sightlines at driveways, crosswalks and intersections (typically 10 m from intersections); not blocking station or emergency egress.
metrics.bad: Furniture blocking sightlines at a driveway or crossing.
metrics.basis: EDM 2026 Chapter 9, p.341 (street furniture); the earlier '1.0 m from crossings and entrances' was not found in 8.4.3, 8.4.9 or Chapter 9.
metrics.method: Check furniture points against driveway, crosswalk and intersection points.

metrics.name: Legacy Fruin level of service cross-check
metrics.good: Level C or better by area per pedestrian (values to be confirmed).
metrics.bad: Level E or F.
metrics.basis: Fruin 1971 and Highway Capacity Manual thresholds were recalled, not opened. TfL says Fruin only assesses crowding, not comfort.
metrics.method: Area per pedestrian from density; map to Fruin classes.

metrics.name: Peak pedestrian generation assumptions
metrics.good: Editable presets by use with low, central and high multipliers, flagged as assumptions.
metrics.bad: Any figure without a source or label.
metrics.basis: No sourced Vancouver trip generation rates were found. Transportation 2040 target of two-thirds of trips on foot, bike or transit by 2040 is context only.
metrics.method: GFA by use times rate times peak-hour share times walk share, times multiplier.

modules.method: For each sidewalk segment adjacent to the site build the width budget: total width minus 0.2 m building buffer, 0.2 m kerb buffer and buffers around trees, poles, benches, racks and canopy posts (TfL method). Distribute person-trips from each entrance (P06-M01), public-lift queues (P06-M07) and station flows (MOBI) onto segments by shortest paths on the P06-M04 walk graph, for peak hour and peak 15 minutes, at low, central and high multipliers. Convert flow to ppmm and map to the PCL class for the area type (Figure 9 row). Report required width for B+ and the shortfall; above 2,000 pph compute width from ppmm. Run crossing-arm and island checks from signal timings. Check Vancouver clear-width and realm-depth standards. Optionally run agent-based simulation.
visualization: Plan view: each sidewalk segment drawn as a ribbon coloured by PCL class (11-class scale from A+ blue to E dark red) with a ppmm legend and the area-type floor marked.
Cross-section bars per segment: building buffer, active zone, clear width, furniture, kerb buffer, with a marker at the width needed for B+.
Line chart of ppmm against hour of day with a low-central-high band, the B+ line and the area-type floor line drawn.
Pass/fail badges linked to TfL and EDM clauses; external-benchmark rows in their own style; assumption presets dashed.
modules.human_judgment: Peak scenario choice (event days, train arrival waves), how to trade clear width against trees, patios and seating, perceived crowding by older people and children, and seasonal or weather effects.
modules.limits: TfL comfort levels come from London footway studies; Vancouver conditions differ. Flow comes from assumption presets, not counts. Cyclists, e-scooters and vehicle crossings are not modelled in the static check. Fruin values are unverified.

modules.name: Inclusive and accessible design at grade
modules.design_question: Can everyone, including wheelchair users, people with low vision and older people, reach and use every public entrance, space and the station link at grade without barriers?
modules.effort: About 5-7 person-days; slope mapping and rest-spacing checks are simple, door and entrance data need annotation.
inputs: Terrain: DEM or spot elevations for the site and surrounding streets (SITE packet)
Layer0 ground slab levels, entrances with threshold heights, stairs, ramps and lifts (tagged objects)
P06-M04 RouteGraph, clear widths and below-grade link lifts and stairs
Seating points from P06-M03; crossing and curb-ramp points
Manual fields: door clear width, automatic openers, tactile surfaces, accessible washrooms
outputs: SlopeMap: raster of running slope (%) and crossfall (%)
StepFreeRoutes: {from_entrance, to_target, step_free, max_slope, max_gap_to_rest_m}[]
RestCoverage: polygons within 50 m, 100 m and 150 m of seating
AccessChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES)

parameters.name: Running slope of public routes
parameters.relationship: Steeper slope -> more effort and need to rest; 5% (1:20) is the City target where achievable, anything steeper is a ramp, and 1:12 is the UK absolute maximum for short runs.

parameters.name: Crossfall
parameters.relationship: Crossfall drains water but makes wheelchairs drift and challenges balance; Vancouver designs 2% (1-4% range), UK guidance prefers 1-2% with 1 in 40 as the maximum.

parameters.name: Level change between sidewalk and slab
parameters.relationship: Bigger grade differences force stairs, ramps or lifts; CDDG says integrate them in the building envelope and keep a visual and physical connection to the public realm.

parameters.name: Clear path width
parameters.relationship: At least 2.0 m lets two wheelchairs pass; 1.5 m lets a wheelchair and a walker pass; 1.0 m at obstacles for no more than 6 m (UK guidance).

parameters.name: Spacing of seats and rest spots
parameters.relationship: Closer rests let more people complete a walk: Vancouver gives 150 m for wheelchair and visually impaired users, 100 m for mobility impaired without a stick, 50 m for stick users.

parameters.name: Landings on slopes
parameters.relationship: Level landings at least every 0.5 m of rise, as long as the ramp is wide, give rest points and allow passing.

parameters.name: Headroom under canopies, stairs and soffits
parameters.relationship: Headroom of at least 2.3 m prevents head strikes by people with low vision; undersides of stairs need a barrier below that height.

parameters.name: Tactile surfaces at flush crossings
parameters.relationship: Flush crossings lack a curb cue; Vancouver requires truncated domes where grade break is under 5%, so layout must leave room for paired bracketing.

parameters.name: Governing building code and standards
parameters.relationship: BC Building Code does not apply in Vancouver; the Vancouver Building By-law and CSA B651 govern barrier-free entrances, ramps and doors. Numeric requirements were not opened.

metrics.name: Running slope of public paths
metrics.good: At most 5% (1:20) where achievable.
metrics.bad: Above 5% where flatter is achievable; steeper runs are ramps needing landings and handrails.
metrics.basis: Engineering Design Manual 2026 (5% maximum running slope where achievable).
metrics.method: Slope from DEM or pathway profile along each route segment.

metrics.name: Ramp gradient, landings and headroom
metrics.good: Ramp at most 1:20 preferred, 1:12 (8.3%) absolute maximum; landing for each 0.5 m of rise; headroom at least 2.3 m.
metrics.bad: Steeper than 1:12, longer runs without landing, or headroom below 2.3 m.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2-4.3: text verified, UK guidance, not adopted by Vancouver; Building By-law and CSA B651 not opened.
metrics.method: Check ramp profiles and soffit heights.

metrics.name: Crossfall
metrics.good: About 2% design, within the EDM 1-4% range.
metrics.bad: Outside 1-4%; amber between 2.5% and 4% on constrained sites (DfT would flag above 2.5%, external comparison).
metrics.basis: EDM 2026 8.4.3.3 (2%, 1-4% range); DfT s4.3 shown only as a comparison.
metrics.method: Cross slope across the sidewalk from the section.

metrics.name: Clear width of public routes
metrics.good: At least 3.0 m on commercial streets; at least 2.4 m on mid-block links.
metrics.bad: Below 2.4 m (constrained minimum), or below 3.0 m on commercial streets without City Engineer agreement.
metrics.basis: EDM Table 8-3; CDDG S3.8.1. DfT 2.0 m desirable footway is an external comparison.
metrics.method: Minimum clear width per route segment from P06-M04.

metrics.name: Obstacle gaps and footway minimum
metrics.good: Footway at least 2.0 m desirable (1.5 m acceptable); gaps at obstacles at least 1.0 m and no longer than 6 m.
metrics.bad: Below 1.5 m anywhere, or below 1.0 m at obstacles longer than 6 m.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2: text verified, not adopted by Vancouver.
metrics.method: Scan route segments for obstacle gaps.

metrics.name: Rest spacing along public routes
metrics.good: A seat or rest spot at most 50 m apart along busy routes; 100-150 m acceptable for other groups.
metrics.bad: Gaps over 150 m.
metrics.basis: EDM 2026 Table 8-2 (research from the late 1980s); DfT s4.5 (50 m) as comparison.
metrics.method: Distance along routes between seating nodes; compare to groups in Table 8-2.

metrics.name: Step-free public entrances
metrics.good: All primary public entrances and the station link step-free from the sidewalk.
metrics.bad: Any public entrance needing a step or a separate back route.
metrics.basis: Vancouver Building By-law Part 3.8 and CSA B651 not opened; target stated as a design intent, to be checked by the code consultant.
metrics.method: Graph routing with step edges removed.

metrics.name: Truncated-dome treatment at flush crossings
metrics.good: Required where grade break between sidewalk and ramp top is under 5%.
metrics.bad: Flush crossing without tactile surface.
metrics.basis: EDM 2026 section 8.4.1.4.
metrics.method: Check each crossing point for grade break and tactile flag.

modules.method: Compute a slope raster from the DEM and site grading, or slope profiles along each route edge from P06-M04. Classify running slope as 0-5% (green), 5-8.3% (amber, ramp) and above 8.3% (red). Measure crossfall from sections. Remove edges with steps from the walk graph to find step-free routes between each public entrance, the sidewalk, the plaza and the station link (lifts from P06-M04 kept). Report any entrance with no step-free route. Place seating nodes and compute the longest gap along each route against the group distances. Check headroom, landings and tactile domes. Compile code items for the code consultant (Vancouver Building By-law, CSA B651) as a manual checklist, not a computed result.
visualization: Ground-plane slope map with three classes (green up to 5%, amber 5-8.3%, red above 8.3%), small arrows for direction of fall and a legend in percent and ratio.
Rest-coverage overlay: 50 m, 100 m and 150 m radius rings around seating nodes, shaded by group.
Step-free route traces from each public entrance to the station link, breaks marked with an X and the clause that fails.
Checklist panel with badges linked to EDM clauses; DfT rows in the external-benchmark style; code items as 'needs consultant' chips.
modules.human_judgment: Lived-experience review with the City's disability advisory groups, wayfinding clarity, sensory and cognitive comfort (glare, noise, complexity), dignity of access (no separate back door), and independent accessibility rating such as Rick Hansen Foundation certification (not opened).
modules.limits: Code compliance cannot be proven from a massing model. Slope needs an elevation model; downtown grade data may need City LiDAR. DfT numbers are UK benchmarks. No door, handrail or washroom geometry exists in Layer 0.
