modules.name: Vertical public realm: public uses at height
modules.design_question: Do public, cultural and civic uses extend up the tower in a way that is genuinely open, visible from the street, reachable and worth visiting, not just a token lobby or ticketed deck?
modules.effort: About 4-5 person-days; reads program tags per storey, access attributes are manual; street lobby and queue check add about 1 day.
inputs: Layer0.ProgramTags per storey: public | cultural_civic | amenity | retail | hotel | office | residential | mechanical | core
Storey heights and areas from Layer 0 massing; crown height
VerticalCirculation tags: lift banks (public or tenant), escalators, stairs, street-level public lift lobby (from advanced presets, or placeholders)
AccessAttributes per public space: free | ticketed | booked, opening hours, covenant yes/no, outdoor or indoor
Terrace and roof polygons flagged public
outputs: VerticalPublicProfile: {storey, height_m, public_gfa_m2, access_regime}[]
PublicShareAboveStreetwall: number (%)
HighestPublicStoreyHeight_m and ratio to total height
MaxGapBetweenPublicLevels: number (storeys and m)
PublicLiftQueue: {persons_peak, area_m2, frontage_m} (consumed by P06-M05)
VerticalPublicChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08, SYST for egress, PRES boards)

parameters.name: Public and cultural share of floor area above the streetwall
parameters.relationship: More public floor area above the podium -> stronger sense that public life reaches up the tower; but each public floor needs separate lifts, security and egress and displaces revenue floors.

parameters.name: Height of the highest public storey
parameters.relationship: A public level near the crown gives skyline and mountain views and a reason to travel up; but the top floors are the most valuable and most exposed to wind.

parameters.name: Vertical gap between public levels
parameters.relationship: Large gaps break the idea that public uses extend vertically; sky lobbies and stacked civic rooms at regular intervals make a legible vertical sequence.

parameters.name: Dedicated public vertical circulation
parameters.relationship: Separate public lifts or escalators keep public access independent of tenants and security, but need lobby space and core area; London policy asks for a separate entrance (not opened).

parameters.name: Street-level public lobby and queue
parameters.relationship: A public lift lobby with its own street frontage makes vertical uses visible and welcoming; its queue can spill onto the sidewalk and cut clear width unless the lobby holds the peak queue.

parameters.name: Access regime and hours
parameters.relationship: Free walk-up access and long hours widen the public; booked or ticketed access narrows it. London's Sky Garden is free with a booked ticket and open until midnight; Vancouver Lookout at Harbour Centre is ticketed.

parameters.name: Size and height of interior public space
parameters.relationship: Rooms of at least about 93 m2 and 9.1 m high read as civic spaces (borrowed from the FSR-exclusion condition); lobbies serving principal entries and circulation do not count.

parameters.name: Outdoor public terraces at height
parameters.relationship: Open-air public terraces add views and weather exposure; wind comfort there comes from the CLIM wind module and may limit hours or types of use.

metrics.name: Public or cultural GFA above the streetwall
metrics.good: At least 5% of above-podium GFA (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Below 1% (editable preset).
metrics.basis: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy asks that, where possible, a building include community-significant uses such as a public observation deck or other public amenity; no number exists. VTC brief asks that public-facing uses extend vertically.
metrics.method: Sum GFA of public and cultural_civic storeys above the podium line divided by total GFA above it.

metrics.name: Distinct public levels above the podium
metrics.good: At least two separated public levels, one in the top quarter of building height (editable preset).
metrics.bad: No public level above the podium.
metrics.basis: No sourced threshold; the preset follows the brief's vertical continuity intent.
metrics.method: Cluster public storeys; count clusters and note the highest.

metrics.name: Maximum gap between public levels
metrics.good: At most one quarter of total height (editable preset).
metrics.bad: More than one half of total height (editable preset).
metrics.basis: Placeholder; no sourced rule.
metrics.method: Difference between consecutive public storey heights, plus ground to first and last to roof.

metrics.name: Interior public space quality floor
metrics.good: At least about 93.0 m2 and about 9.1 m clear height, secured by covenant.
metrics.bad: Smaller or lower, or secured only by lease; lobbies for principal entries and circulation are excluded.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] CDDG S3.3.1 is a condition for FSR exclusion of interior public space, not a quality floor for sky-level rooms; the transfer is ours. Glossary excludes principal-entry lobbies.
metrics.method: Check area and floor-to-ceiling height of tagged public rooms.

metrics.name: Street visibility and access of public uses
metrics.good: Public uses have direct visual and physical access from the sidewalk (street-level lobby or frontage), not only through a tenant lobby.
metrics.bad: Hidden behind tenant lobby or reached only by a service route.
metrics.basis: CDDG G3.3.3 asks direct visual and physical access from the sidewalk for interior public space; G3.3.1 invites it in major Business District developments.
metrics.method: Check each public vertical node for a street-level frontage or lobby tag and a sightline from the sidewalk.

metrics.name: Public-lift queue spill-over
metrics.good: Reported only: peak queue persons and the lobby area that holds them, passed to P06-M05; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: Queue area exceeds the lobby and spills onto the sidewalk.
metrics.basis: Lift capacity belongs to SYST and MOBI; no sourced queue-area standard was opened.
metrics.method: Peak public occupant load per lift cycle divided into lobby area; compare with sidewalk clear width in M05.

metrics.name: Public access hours and cost at height
metrics.good: Free, open to the public from at least 10:00 to 22:00, seven days (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Office hours only, ticketed, or by invitation.
metrics.basis: Sky Garden London is free with booking and opens to midnight (precedent); Vancouver Lookout is ticketed. The City memo of April 2026 treats ticketed Lookout access as typical. The 2002 staff report judged a hotel lobby plus roof garden an inadequate public amenity.
metrics.method: Read access attributes per public node.

metrics.name: Public vertical circulation
metrics.good: Dedicated public lifts or an independent public lobby with its own entrance (preset).
metrics.bad: Public level reached only via tenant lobby.
metrics.basis: Based on London Plan Policy D9 intent, which was not opened (Cloudflare challenge).
metrics.method: Check circulation tags for separation.

modules.method: Read the storey table from Layer 0 and tag each storey by public, cultural or civic programme and area. Identify the podium line from the first tower step-back (shared with P06-M02). Compute public share of floor area above the podium, number and positions of public clusters, vertical gaps, height of the highest public storey, and area and clear height of each interior public room. Read access attributes (free, ticketed, hours, covenant) from each public node and the circulation tags to test separation from tenant lifts and street visibility. Estimate the public-lift queue and pass it to P06-M05. Compare with the threshold table and mark each result verified, team assumption or unverified. Pass public occupant demand to SYST (egress) and MOBI (lift capacity).
visualization: Vertical strip diagram: tower elevation as a column from 0 to total height in metres, one band per storey coloured by programme, public storeys outlined with a heavy stroke, lift lines drawn, markers at the highest public storey and the podium line.
Per-node 24-hour clock-arc showing opening hours and a chip for free, booked or ticketed.
Street-level plan of the public lift lobby with its frontage, queue area and the sidewalk clear width beside it.
Histogram of public GFA per 10-storey band; pass/fail badges linked to CDDG clauses and the preset table; derived rows dashed.
modules.human_judgment: Whether the space is welcoming rather than token, programme curation and cultural content (including Indigenous perspectives), cost and security screening, equity of access, management, and safety and egress for large public loads at height.
modules.limits: Threshold presets have no sourced value; only CDDG G3.3.3 and precedents are cited, and the 93 m2 room floor is a derived transfer. Life-safety, lift capacity and wind comfort at height belong to other packets. Access regime is user-entered. CTBUH material was not opened (403).

modules.name: Gehl-type public-life triage: what can be computed and what needs people
modules.design_question: Which of Gehl's twelve public-space quality criteria can the tool compute from the massing, which only through proxies, and which need human audit or field observation?
modules.effort: About 4-6 person-days for the triage matrix, count bars and manual audit form; agent-based public-life prediction is roadmap.
inputs: Check outputs of P06-M01 to P06-M07 (pass, amber, fail with source badges)
CLIM: sun, wind, rain-shelter and noise results (if available)
ECOL: tree canopy and planting (if available)
Manual audit form (microscale streetscape audit items, exclusionary-feature checklist) filled by team members
Optional baseline: public-life counts of the existing site (Gehl-style stationary activity and movement counts)
outputs: CriteriaTriage: {criterion, group, mode: computed | proxy | human | field, pass_n, amber_n, fail_n, confidence}[12]
PublicLifeProfile: counts per criterion with computed and judged rows distinguished (no score)
PlaceDiagramMap: mapping of results to four place qualities
Gaps: list of criteria still without evidence (for the policy reflection board)

parameters.name: Roll-up rule (counts only)
parameters.relationship: Showing pass, amber and fail counts per criterion keeps the 40% human-scale jury weight visible without inventing weights between criteria; no validated weighting exists, so no 0-100 score or composite is produced.

parameters.name: Evidence mode per criterion
parameters.relationship: A criterion moves from 'human' to 'proxy' to 'computed' as the tool gains data; shows what remains judgment and keeps the scorecard honest.

parameters.name: Audit item set (microscale audit)
parameters.relationship: Structured audit items (for example MAPS-Global) make human ratings repeatable between raters; reported inter-rater reliability was mostly 'excellent' in a Japanese online-audit study.

parameters.name: Exclusionary-feature checklist
parameters.relationship: Seat dividers, spikes, gates and sloped ledges signal who is unwelcome; auditing them gives a partial, human-rated proxy for 'who is welcome'. CDDG G3.1.1c asks grilles and gates permeable at all hours.

parameters.name: Baseline public-life counts
parameters.relationship: Counts of people moving and staying before and after a design show real effect; they cannot come from a massing model and are post-occupancy or existing-site work.

metrics.name: Protection against traffic and accidents
metrics.good: Mode proxy: counts of checks on vehicle and bike crossings (M01), crossing and corner comfort and widths (M05); street speeds need SITE data.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: Criteria list recalled from Cities for People, not opened: UNVERIFIED.
metrics.method: Count linked check statuses; show mode and confidence; no score.

metrics.name: Protection against crime and violence
metrics.good: Mode proxy: active frontage, transparency, night activation, blank runs and grilles (M01); lighting needs human input.
metrics.bad: Long blank runs, no night uses.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened. CDDG G3.1.1 supports passive security by lighting, transparency and activity.
metrics.method: Count linked M01 checks plus manual lighting rating.

metrics.name: Protection against unpleasant sensory experiences (wind, rain, noise, pollution)
metrics.good: Mode computed for wind (CLIM) and shelter (M01); noise and air need other models.
metrics.bad: Strolling-class wind at seating or no weather protection.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened. CDDG S4.11.1 noise levels cover residential rooms and amenity space only, so no public-realm noise number exists.
metrics.method: Count wind-point and shelter checks; mark noise and air as gaps.

metrics.name: Opportunities to walk
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: clear widths and PCL (M05), slopes (M06), directness (M04); edge quality is human.
metrics.bad: Clear width below standard.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Count linked M04-M06 checks; manual edge rating.

metrics.name: Opportunities to stand and stay
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: edge depth, plaza edges, seating at edges (M01, M03); quality of the edge zone is human.
metrics.bad: No edge zones or seating at edges.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Count linked M01 and M03 checks; manual edge-zone rating.

metrics.name: Opportunities to sit
metrics.good: Mode computed: seating supply, sun and wind at seating (M03); seat comfort and exclusionary features are human.
metrics.bad: No seating or no sun on seating.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened; seating benchmark is NYC (external).
metrics.method: Count M03 seating, sun and wind checks; audit exclusionary features.

metrics.name: Opportunities to see
metrics.good: Mode proxy: sightlines and transparency (M01, M04, optional isovist); interest of views is human.
metrics.bad: Blocked sightlines or blank edges.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Count linked checks; optional isovist area from key points.

metrics.name: Opportunities to hear and talk
metrics.good: Mode human or field: needs an acoustic model or on-site observation.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened; no public-realm noise threshold found.
metrics.method: Manual audit entries only.

metrics.name: Opportunities to play and exercise
metrics.good: Mode human: programme and facilities are judgments; POPS size and shape (M03) are inputs only.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Manual audit entries; link M03 geometry as context.

metrics.name: Scale
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: podium band, unit rhythm and massing variation (M01, M02); perception needs a human check.
metrics.bad: Podium outside the band or unit frontage beyond range.
metrics.basis: Criterion wording not opened; the linked CDDG checks are verified. Gehl dictionary (opened) defines human scale as dimensions relating to the human body and eye-level experience.
metrics.method: Count linked M01 and M02 checks; manual perception rating.

metrics.name: Opportunities to enjoy positive aspects of climate
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: sun hours (M03), shelter (M01), wind class; trees from ECOL; comfort in use is human.
metrics.bad: Shaded, windy plaza with no planting.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened; PPS Place Diagram (opened) lists sun or shade under comfort and image.
metrics.method: Count M03 sun, M01 shelter and wind checks; manual rating.

metrics.name: Positive sensory experiences
metrics.good: Mode human: materials, detailing, views and planting quality; ECOL canopy is an input only.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Manual audit entries; link ECOL canopy as context.

metrics.name: Share of criteria with computed or proxy evidence
metrics.good: Reported as a count out of 12; preset target at least 6 of 12 by 10 Dec 2026.
metrics.bad: Fewer than 4 of 12.
metrics.basis: Project management measure, not a design threshold.
metrics.method: Count criteria whose mode is computed or proxy.

modules.method: Create a 12-row matrix, one row per criterion, grouped protection (3), comfort (6) and delight (3). For each row record the evidence mode (computed, proxy, human audit, field observation) and link the module checks used. Pull checks from P06-M01 to P06-M07 and show pass, amber and fail counts with source badges. Never convert to 0-100 or a composite: the 40% human-scale jury weight stays at category level. For human rows present a short audit form from a microscale streetscape audit, with rater initials and date and an exclusionary-feature checklist. Draw counts per row, computed rows solid and judged rows hatched. Cross-map to the PPS Place Diagram (opened). Mark the criteria list UNVERIFIED until Cities for People or another Gehl source is opened.
visualization: Twelve rows grouped protection, comfort and delight; each row a stacked bar of pass, amber and fail counts; computed rows solid, proxy dotted, human hatched, field-only empty with a dashed ring; no total.
Triage matrix: rows are criteria, columns are computed / proxy / human audit / field data, with the source module and clause linked in each cell.
Four-quadrant Place Diagram overlay (access and linkages, uses and activities, comfort and image, sociability) with counts of evidence per quadrant.
Badge 'Human-scale experience: 40% of jury' on the profile; FALSE ASSUMPTION colour for any retracted rating.
modules.human_judgment: Almost all 'delight' criteria, edge quality, seat comfort, perceived safety, who feels welcome, noise tolerance, cultural meaning and inclusion. Field counts and surveys can only be done on a built or existing place. The scorecard exists to mark that boundary.
modules.limits: Gehl's criteria wording and any quantity (door counts, viewing distances) were recalled, not opened, so no Gehl numbers are used as thresholds. No validated composite exists. Proxies measure the model, not behaviour; counts of people need field work.

flags.claim: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is the policy that frames 244-305 m (800-1,000 ft) towers on the VTC site.
flags.correction: The City's April 2026 memo says the policy was last updated in 2011 and currently allows up to 600 ft (about 183 m), with one location up to 700 ft (about 213 m). The VTC height range is above it. The review is open and draft directions are expected in late 2026.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S04, P06-S03. VTC heights are hypothetical beyond current policy; the 1997 criteria on public amenity, open space and microclimate (P06-S05) are used here as the policy intent.

flags.claim: The Downtown (Except Downtown South) Design Guidelines and Central Area Pedestrian Weather Protection guidelines govern podium, streetwall and ground-floor design for Central Business District sites.
flags.correction: Council approved the City-wide Design and Development Guidelines on 28 July 2026 and repealed both documents effective 27 October 2026. The CDDG now governs; its final text was not yet posted. CDDG 4.18 still refers Downtown sites to the DD Character Area Descriptions.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S01 (Appendix B, 4.18), P06-S02. Use CDDG clause numbers, not legacy guideline numbers, in all source badges.

flags.claim: Vancouver requires a numeric ground-floor transparency percentage.
flags.correction: The CDDG asks for transparent glazing across most of the ground-floor facade up to the second-floor underside or canopy underside, with no percentage. Any percentage in the tool is a team assumption.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S3.1.1b).

flags.claim: Downtown solar rules prohibit any new shadow on all public spaces between 10:00 and 16:00 PDT.
flags.correction: The Downtown Peninsula guidelines are tiered: no new shadow on parks, school sites and the Davie and Robson Village north sidewalks; urban plazas and miniparks to be minimised; exceptions through a rationale, 15-minute solar budget and detailed study. Time wording amended from PDT to PT on 28 July 2026.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S09, P06-S01 (Appendix D), P06-S10.

flags.claim: New shadow on urban plazas only needs to be 'actively minimised' (P06-M03 protected-space metric).
flags.correction: Dilawri Square South, Jack Poole Plaza and Robson Square follow 3.1 (no new shadow, 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00, exception path 3.1.2). Dr Sun Yat-Sen Gardens and Park: no new shadow 10:00-16:00 (4.1.1). Victory Square: 3.1 plus the Cenotaph circle 10:00-12:00 on 11 Nov (4.3.1). Other urban plazas and West End miniparks: minimise where possible (3.2.1).
flags.detail: Source: P06-S09 Appendix A (clean text) sections 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.3, Table 1. The earlier packet read the redline, which mixes struck and inserted text.

flags.claim: Vancouver's shadow test is the 10:00-16:00 run in 15-minute steps.
flags.correction: Every Downtown applicant submits a Basic study at two-hour intervals (5.1.1). The 15-minute Detailed study with area take-offs and the coverage formula is for applicants seeking a relaxation of 3.1.1 or 3.3.1 (5.2.1).
flags.detail: Source: P06-S09 Appendix A section 5. The tool offers both studies, Basic by default.

flags.claim: The 10% public open space target for mid-sized sites (S1.9.2) is a valid passing target for the VTC block.
flags.correction: S1.9.2 does not apply: the CDDG glossary defines mid-sized sites as over 4,000 and under 8,000 m2, and the VTC block is about 11,468 m2. Default to S1.9.1 (20%), with POPS of about 10% (S1.10.2) counted inside it.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S01 (glossary, S1.9.1, S1.9.2, S1.10.2), P06-S37 (large-site trigger 8,000 m2 in the 2013 report; current policy not opened).

flags.claim: Mid-block connections of 5.4 m (non-residential), 7.3 m or 4.5 m (half share) are acceptable on the VTC block.
flags.correction: S1.12.2c requires 9.1 m face to face for large sites or sites identified in S1.12.1, and S1.12.1b covers sites adjacent to or including a transit station entrance, which the VTC brief requires. Narrower widths only as a G1.12.1 variation.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S1.12.1, S1.12.2, G1.12.1, S3.8.1). Checked in the CDDG text in r1.

flags.claim: CDDG Table 1.5 tower separation is employment-employment 15.2, employment-hotel 15.2, employment-residential 18.3 and residential-residential 24.4 m.
flags.correction: The table also sets residential-hotel at 24.4 m (reducible to 18.3 m under S1.5.2) and hotel-hotel at 15.2 m; G1.5.1 asks for more separation where towers exceed typical heights. Use the full matrix with S1.5.2 and S1.5.3 conditions.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S1.5.1-S1.5.4, G1.5.1-G1.5.2, Table 1.5). Separation is shared equally between tower sites (S1.5.1).

flags.claim: CDDG S2.2.8 allows 21.3 m podiums only for residential or other listed exceptions.
flags.correction: S2.2.8b also allows 21.3 m on sites with frontage over 60.7 m where enhanced open space is provided; the VTC block frontage (79.2 m and 144.8 m) meets the frontage test.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S2.2.7, S2.2.8, glossary 'Enhanced open space'). Which of S2.2.6 or S2.2.7 governs a mixed tower is unresolved.

flags.claim: Transport interchanges and tourist areas tolerate less crowding than residential streets (TfL).
flags.correction: TfL Figure 9: high street and tourist attraction are strictest (acceptable to B, at risk B-, unacceptable from C+); residential is intermediate (acceptable to B-, at risk C+); office/retail and transport interchange are most tolerant (acceptable to C+, at risk C-). B+ is recommended for all; C+ is the floor with compensation.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S16 p.14. Read from the figure's colour fills by pixel sampling; the round-1 critic's reading (high street most tolerant) does not match, so a visual check is advised.

flags.claim: TfL Appendix B gives 5.3 m total footway width for any flow above 1,200 pph.
flags.correction: TfL says 5.3 m (or 3.3 m without furniture) gives comfortable movement up to 2,000 pph. Above that, derive the clear width from ppmm at B+ (pph / 60 / 11) plus buffers.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S16 Appendix B (p.25), text read.

flags.claim: Solar tests run in 'local Pacific time', with seasonal PST/PDT switching.
flags.correction: Council report RTS 18459 states BC adopted permanent year-round daylight-saving time, and Appendix D replaces PDT with PT. The guidelines set the model to PDT (UTC-7). Use UTC-7 year-round and show the offset; Victory Square 4.3.1 still says PST (unresolved).
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S01 p.5 and Appendix D, P06-S09 section 5.

flags.claim: The City EDM requires street furniture at least 1.0 m from vehicle crossings and entrances.
flags.correction: No 1.0 m figure was found in EDM 8.4.3, 8.4.9 or Chapter 9. EDM p.341 asks furniture to be set back to keep sightlines at driveways and crosswalks, typically 10 m from intersections.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S11. The 1.0 m figure is removed; no replacement number is claimed.

flags.claim: CDDG clause values (entrances, podium bands, tower separation, floorplates, open space targets) are final.
flags.detail: The only text read is draft Appendix A in the Council report. The City says final guidelines will be posted. Table 2.2b was rebuilt from PDF text coordinates. Recheck every CDDG number after posting.

flags.detail: The Gehl People site, its dictionary and Wikipedia do not list the criteria; the book was not opened. No Gehl figure is used as a threshold; criteria names are recalled and flagged. City entrance spacing (8-12 m) is the verified substitute.

flags.detail: The BC page says BC codes do not apply in Vancouver; the by-law text and CSA standard were not opened. Numeric accessibility metrics come from the City EDM and the UK DfT guide.

flags.detail: The London Authority site blocked access. The policy is not used for any number; it appears only as a flagged reference.

flags.claim: Pedestrian wind comfort criteria at grade (seating, entrances, sidewalks, transit plaza, links, terraces).
flags.detail: No Vancouver or other wind criterion was opened. CDDG G1.8.1b is qualitative. Thresholds and mitigation effect of podium, canopy and step-back geometry belong to CLIM; P06 shows results as unverified until CLIM sources exist.

flags.claim: Current text of the Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments (large-site trigger).
flags.detail: The policy PDF was not opened. The 8,000 m2 site or 45,000 m2 floor-area trigger is read in the 2013 Council report only (P06-S37); the VTC block (11,468 m2) meets the site test on that text.

flags.claim: TfL Figure 9 area-type matrix as decoded in the tool.
flags.detail: Read by sampling the colour fills of the PDF page and matching labels by position, not by eye. Confirm visually before the matrix is shown as a source badge.

flags.detail: The ODP map sits on bylaws.vancouver.ca and could not be read. CDDG 4.18 sends Downtown sites to the DD C-5, C-6, HA-1 or HA-2 Character Area Descriptions, or to the Granville Street Plan; neither was opened. The user selects the policy area in SITE.

flags.detail: Glossary sends large sites to the Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments; the 2013 report gives an 8,000 m2 site trigger, which the block meets, but the current text is unopened. POPS is a public open space (glossary), so it counts inside the 20%; whether S1.10.2 is extra is unconfirmed.

flags.detail: Appendix D replaces PDT with PT but leaves 'PST' in 4.3.1. At 10:00 on 11 Nov the sun is 12.6 degrees up at UTC-7 and 18.3 at UTC-8; the tool runs both until the City confirms.

flags.claim: Whether the 3.1.2 exception path applies to Dr Sun Yat-Sen Gardens and Park (4.1.1).
flags.detail: 4.1.1 says 'despite' 3.1 and states no exception. The tool marks it FAIL with no exception chip; ask City planners.

flags.detail: S2.2.8 cross-refers to S2.2.6 though S2.2.7 sets the lower cap. The tool applies the stricter value and shows the S2.2.8 path as an option. Table 2.2b 'Other contexts' column read as 15.2 m for all rows from cell positions.

flags.detail: Editable presets in P06-M01 and P06-M02 without a Vancouver numeric source; the 9.1 m depth borrows G2.10.2c as an analogue; office and residential lobbies default semi-active. Shown dashed with an editable chip.

flags.claim: Sun test of 2 hours on 50% of POPS area, access-hour presets, route directness 1.25/1.5, 100 m block-gap, two lifts on the below-grade link, vertical-public presets (5% GFA, two levels, gap, 10:00-22:00), pedestrian generation rates.

flags.claim: Walking speed for isochrones, peak-hour share of daily trips, peak 15-minute surge proxy and low/central/high demand multipliers.
flags.detail: Editable defaults; Transportation 2040 (two-thirds of trips on foot, bike or transit by 2040) is context only. TfL's average-of-maximum multiplier was not opened.

flags.claim: Status mapping: external benchmarks and derived values are stored as team_assumption with a [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] or [DERIVED] basis prefix.
flags.detail: The output schema allows only verified, team_assumption, unverified and false_assumption_corrected. 'verified' is kept for City of Vancouver text. Recommend adding external_benchmark and derived statuses to the platform.

flags.claim: Performance budget: protected-space shadow projection for 25 instants and about 200 context buildings completes in under 30 s in a laptop browser.
flags.detail: Not benchmarked. Polygon projection replaces a 0.5 m ray grid, which at a 1.35 km radius would be about 23 million cells per instant (about 570 million over 25 instants).

unresolved_relationships: Quantified link between active-frontage percentage or entrance density and pedestrian volume, dwell time and perceived safety: no opened source (Gehl, Ewing and Handy 2009 not opened).
Podium height, canopy and step-back geometry to ground-level wind downwash and sidewalk sunlight: direction is clear but no opened source gives a threshold or effect size; belongs to CLIM.
Acceptable level of sky view factor or enclosure ratio on a downtown street: only CDDG-derived podium ratios (about 0.55-0.75) are available; no literature threshold opened.
Acceptable share of added shadow area: staff say 5-15% is typical for high-rises but explicitly set no benchmark; the tool treats any added shadow on no-new-shadow spaces as a breach.
Effect of public floors at height on lift demand, security cost and revenue: no opened source; London D9 and CTBUH material not opened.
Pedestrian generation rates by programme and walk share for the VTC site, and the surge multiplier from hourly flow to peak 15 minutes or TfL average-of-maximum: no Vancouver source opened.
Vancouver hours-of-access rule for POPS under SRW agreements; only the NYC rule was opened.
Route directness and block-length thresholds that predict walking; only a connectivity-physical activity association (children) was opened.
Wind comfort thresholds at seating, entrances, sidewalks, transit plaza, links and terraces: to be taken from CLIM with its own sources.
Whether CDDG S1.10.2 (POPS about 10%) is extra to or inside S1.9.1 (20%), and how park dedication interacts; glossary counts POPS as public open space.
Required width, daylight and lift count of the below-grade station link relative to ridership: CDDG gives only 'an elevator and staircase'; TransLink standards not opened.
